speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked	the Minister for Health (a) whether the Ministry will review the grant to help families hire foreign domestic workers to care for elderly persons with disabilities; (b) how many households are currently receiving this grant; and (c) what is the Government's annual expenditure on this grant since it was introduced in 2012.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Besides the FDW Grant, these households are also eligible for FDW concessionary levy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Pioneers can get additional cash payouts to help with their expenses through the Pioneer Generation-Disability Assistance Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We also have other financial schemes to help defray the cost of caring for the elderly with more severe disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Examples include the Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly (IDAPE) and ElderShield, which is a disability insurance scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We will continue to monitor the utilisation and adequacy of the FDW Grant.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am asking the question in the context of my constituency where there is an increasing number of elderly and elderly residents with disabilities as well.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My supplementary question  is: will the Ministry consider waiving the concessionary levy altogether for the elderly who are aged above 80 or 85, for example?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The FDW concessionary levy for those with caregiving needs was just reduced from $120 a month to $60 a month in May 2015, which was less than a year ago.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And as I said earlier in my reply, this is significantly lower than the regular FDW levy of $265.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This will benefit families with children aged below 16, elderly aged 65 and above or disabled family members.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, if these frail elderly are aged 80 or above, the likelihood would be that they would belong to the Pioneer Generation, so they will also be able to receive cash payouts of $1,200 a year under the Pioneer Generation Disability Assistance Scheme.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Having said that, we will continue to review the schemes to better support families with care-giving needs, including those with elderly dependants.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Would a Singaporean be eligible for the grant if the elderly parent is a non-citizen?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If the elderly parent is aged 65 and above and is a Permanent Resident, they can still get the grant as long as the caregiver is a Singaporean.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: The non-citizen I am referring to is a foreigner.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The grant is given if the frail elderly is a Permanent Resident and aged above 65.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Having said that, this is one of the many available schemes we have to support elderly with caregiving needs.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: The foreigner has to be a Permanent Resident, Mr Zainal Sapari.
